title: Fig and blackcurrant soy candle
subtitle: A deep, fruity soy wax jar candle
excerpt: A deep, fruity soy wax jar candle fragranced with fig and blackcurrant fragrance oils at 7% of wax weight. Fig gives a green, milky note; blackcurrant adds a tart, dark-berry depth that rounds the combination out. Pour into a 200 ml glass jar and cure five to seven days before lighting.
sourceNotes: Fig fragrance oil flash point: typically >65°C (supplier SDS, Bramble Berry 2023). Blackcurrant fragrance oil flash point: typically >60°C. Both are above the 55°C pour temperature if using the lower-temp pour approach; 65°C is safe for most suppliers, check the SDS for the specific lot. 7% combined fragrance load at or below the maximum capacity for container soy wax.

recipe.batchNotes: Pour multiple jars from a single melt. Maintain the 7% fragrance load.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cure five to seven days. The fig-blackcurrant combination develops a clean, fruity-green scent during the cure.
recipe.temperatureNote: Pour at 60 to 65°C. Verify the flash points of your specific fragrance oils before adding.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Two years in a cool, dry cupboard. Fruity fragrance notes fade somewhat faster than woody or resinous notes; keep the lid on between uses.

glossaryTerms.definition: The temperature at which a fragrance oil can ignite if exposed to a flame. Always check the supplier SDS for your specific fragrance oil and add it to wax that is below the stated flash point.
The first burn of a jar candle. Burn until the melt pool reaches the jar edge before extinguishing, to prevent tunnelling on subsequent burns.
The resting period after pouring. Five to seven days allows the fragrance to bind into the wax matrix and develop full scent throw.
